result.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
result.summary: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet visual corruption can disrupt the resulting policies. We introduce HOG-WAM, which adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as structural supervision derived directly from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer (DiT) module reads RGB features through asymmetric attention, allowing its objective to shape the visual representation used for control. The module is used only during training and removed at inference, preserving FastWAM's RGB-to-action architecture. We evaluate four controlled observation corruptions through a visual-corruption extension of RoboTwin, termed RoboTwin-Plus; HOG-WAM achieves the highest success among the compared policies under all four. Mixed-noise success increases from 78.86% to 82.86% relative to FastWAM, with comparable performance on clean scenes. On LIBERO Plus, overall success increases from 74.49% to 75.26%, with the largest gain under sensor noise, from 74.14% to 78.89%. Across four Franka tasks, average success increases from 40% to 59% under clean observations and from 17% to 24% under noisy observations. A representation ablation favors combining RGB observations with auxiliary HOG prediction over replacing RGB with HOG. These findings support future-gradient prediction as complementary supervision for visually robust control, with larger absolute gains on physical tasks than in simulation. Code is available at https://github.com/iPPLab/HOG-WAM.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 HOG-WAM，在机器人 world-action 模型训练时用未来 HOG 预测作为辅助监督，通过非对称注意力塑造视觉表示，并在推理时移除该模块，以提升视觉损坏下的控制鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其训练期辅助监督直接作用于供控制使用的视觉表示，可能为 LVR 中保留视觉细节、抑制视觉旁路提供可核查线索；但研究的是机器人策略而非多模态推理，需较多迁移判断。
